title: A Growing Row
statement: A row contains $41$ numbers. The first number plus the second is $3$, the second plus the third is $6$, and the third plus the fourth is $9$. This pattern continues, with each sum of two neighbouring numbers being $3$ more than the sum before it, up to the sum of the $40$th and $41$st numbers. What is the value of the $41$st number minus the $1$st number?
hints: Write the first number, the second number and the third number as $a$, $b$ and $c$, so that $a + b = 3$ and $b + c = 6$. Which number appears in both sums?
Subtract one neighbouring sum from the next. The number the two sums share cancels, which leaves a difference between two numbers that are two places apart in the row.
Subtracting any neighbouring sum from the next shows that moving two places along the row always adds exactly $3$. Now count how many moves of two places take you from position $1$ to position $41$.
solution: Call the numbers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{41}$. The sums start at $3$ and go up by $3$ each time, so the $k$th sum is $3k$: $$a_k + a_{k+1} = 3k \quad \text{for } 1 \le k \le 40.$$ These equations do not fix the individual numbers, since $a_1$ can be chosen freely and the rest then follow. We therefore look for the difference directly. For $1 \le k \le 39$, subtract the $k$th equation from the next one. The shared number $a_{k+1}$ cancels, which gives $$a_{k+2} - a_k = 3(k + 1) - 3k = 3.$$ So moving two places along the row always adds exactly $3$. Positions $1$ and $41$ are both odd, so we can go from one to the other in moves of two places: $1 \to 3 \to 5 \to \cdots \to 41$. Since $41 - 1 = 40$ and each move covers two places, there are $20$ moves, not $40$. Each move is an instance of the result above, with $k = 1, 3, \ldots, 39$. Now write the required difference as a sum in which each intermediate term appears once with each sign and so cancels: $$a_{41} - a_1 = (a_3 - a_1) + (a_5 - a_3) + \cdots + (a_{41} - a_{39}) = 20 \cdot 3.$$ The $41$st number minus the $1$st number is $60$. Why this works. linear-combination-of-equations, telescoping: subtracting neighbouring sums removes the shared number, and the resulting equal differences add up along the row while the intermediate numbers cancel.
